metadata.title: Dataset and artifacts for "Too Many Reports, Too Few Handovers: A Large-Scale Study of Configuration Inefficiencies in Operational 5G Networks"
metadata.description:
Measurement data and analysis artifacts for the CoNEXT 2026 paper Too Many Reports, Too Few Handovers: A Large-Scale Study of Configuration Inefficiencies in Operational 5G Networks (Proc. ACM Netw. 4, CoNEXT4, Article 64, 10.1145/3856978).

The dataset comes from four cross-country driving campaigns across the United States between August 2022 and November 2024, covering 15,000+ km and all three major US operators (AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon), both LTE and 5G, both 5G architectures (NSA and SA), and all 5G frequency bands. Measurements were collected with XCAL Solo.

Merged measurement data — one tarball per campaign, 17,771 measurement runs and 16,508,113 rows in total. Each tarball holds a single Python pickle containing a list of pandas DataFrames, one per run, joining the per-second PHY/KPI series, the signalling flow and the RRC message log, plus parser-derived Handover_*, Measconfig_* and MeasurementReport_* columns carrying the handover configurations the paper analyses.

  • trip1_2022_all_df.tar.gz — 2022-08-07 to 2022-08-15, 5,921 runs
  • trip2_2023_all_df.tar.gz — 2023-05-13 to 2023-05-16, 1,064 runs
  • trip3_2023_all_df.tar.gz — 2023-08-05 to 2023-08-08, 8,632 runs
  • trip4_2024_all_df.tar.gz — 2024-11-01 to 2024-11-08, 2,154 runs

Processed data — derived tables the figures are computed from. The tiers are cumulative, so download only the one matching the figures you want to regenerate.

  • processed_bundle_small.tar.gz (1.1 MB) — Figures 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9
  • processed_bundle_medium.tar.gz (123 MB) — adds Figure 6
  • processed_bundle_full.tar.gz (1.1 GB) — adds the inputs for Figures 2, 10–16 and 18

SHA256SUMS.txt covers every tarball; verify before unpacking.

Analysis and figure-generation code: github.com/NUWiNS/conext26-handover-paper-dataset. See merged/README.md there for the data model and a reference to the 840 columns, and MANIFEST.md for which script produces each figure from which tier.

Note: the data ships as Python pickles, which are sensitive to library versions. Use the pins in requirements.txt (Python 3.10, numpy 2.2.2, pandas 2.3.1). Timestamp is float64 Unix epoch seconds: parsing it without specifying the unit silently yields 1970 dates.
